supporting_observations.claim: At 13:44:34 UTC, ana.ruiz ran PowerShell to compress \\FILE-PIN-01\Shared\Clients into C:\Users\ana.ruiz\AppData\Local\Temp\c.zip; Sysmon then recorded creation of that archive.

At 13:50:57 UTC, the proxy recorded a 51,000,000-byte client-to-server transfer from WS-ARUIZ-01 to the unapproved dropzone-transfer.net service. A corresponding proxy connection record reports 51,000,372 originating bytes, and Sysmon attributes the connection to Firefox running as ana.ruiz.

The archive of the Shared\Clients directory shortly before a large outbound transfer to an unapproved file-transfer service strongly supports suspected data exfiltration, although the logs do not directly establish that the transferred payload was c.zip.

known_telemetry_limitations: The available records show transfer size, destination, user, and client process, but do not expose the transferred payload or prove it was the archive.

The alert describes activity around 13:46 UTC, while the supplied records show the large transfer at 13:50:57 UTC; the evidence does not establish whether this timing difference reflects an approximate alert time or a separate event.
claims_not_established: That c.zip, or any specific client data, was the payload sent to dropzone-transfer.net.
The identity or intent of the recipient, or whether the transfer was authorized by the organization.
Whether the alert's stated 13:46 time corresponds to the 13:50:57 transfer in the records.
additional_evidence_needed: Endpoint evidence for c.zip, including its contents, size, hash, and any file-access or deletion activity.
Proxy or network records that identify the transferred object, request method, destination path, and complete transfer timing.
User and business-owner confirmation of whether the Shared\Clients archive and use of dropzone-transfer.net were authorized.
unrelated_findings: Dropbox.exe ran on WS-ARUIZ-01 and connected to desktop.dropbox.com; Dropbox is not among the organization's approved services. Track separately; it does not by itself establish the payload or destination of the alerted transfer. (T099-00239, T099-00247)
ana.ruiz, a non-IT-administrator, ran PowerShell Get-ADUser against the IT OU. This is separate from the alerted transfer and should be reviewed independently. (T099-00433, T099-00434)
